oneLine: Takes a shopper's order at checkout with a confirmed delivery promise for every shipment group, and follows each group until it is delivered, lost, returned or cancelled.

rows.title: Register a shopper
rows.story: A shopper is registered with an e-mail, which can be used only once, and may start with saved delivery addresses. This is a test shopper, with no real account behind it.

rows.title: Save a delivery address
rows.story: A shopper saves an address to reuse at checkout, up to twenty. At checkout the address is copied into the order, so later edits never change a placed order.

rows.title: Place an order
rows.story: Checkout makes and confirms a delivery promise for each shipment group, and only then stores the order. If an offer is stale, nothing is placed and fresh offers come back. Nothing is placed if delivery-promise is down.

then.does: queues one assignment for each shipment group

rows.title: Release holds a failed checkout left behind
rows.story: If a later group fails to confirm, the promises already confirmed are cancelled. A cancel that itself fails is queued and retried until delivery-promise lets the capacity go.
rows.policy: Every pass, retry the promise cancels a failed checkout could not perform

then.does: cancels the confirmed promise and returns its capacity

rows.title: Ask to cancel an order
rows.story: The shopper asks to cancel every group not yet locked. It is a request: the group waits until order-sourcing answers, and a vendor that ships first wins.

then.does: cancels each group not yet locked, or refuses it
cancels the promises of the cancelled groups

rows.title: Cancel a group whose promise cannot be kept
rows.story: When delivery-promise finds no route that can still deliver, the group is cancelled at once rather than left open.
rows.policy: Whenever a promise is unkeepable, cancel its shipment group

then.does: cancels the group's assignment, or refuses it if already locked

rows.title: Accept a cancellation
rows.story: order-sourcing confirms it cancelled the group. The group, and the order if nothing else remains, becomes Cancelled.
rows.policy: Whenever order-sourcing cancels a group, mark the group cancelled

rows.title: Accept a refusal to cancel
rows.story: If the group was already locked, order-sourcing refuses. The group goes back to Locked and the vendor ships.
rows.policy: Whenever order-sourcing refuses a cancel, put the group back to locked

rows.title: Follow a revised promise
rows.story: When delivery-promise moves a promise to a later window, the group's delivery window, ship-by and node move with it. A revision no newer than the stored one changes nothing.
rows.policy: Whenever a promise is revised, move the group's window to the new one

rows.title: Record the promise verdict
rows.story: The tracking view shows whether the promise was kept or broken, and by how many minutes. An at-risk promise shows its reason the same way.
rows.policy: Whenever a promise is kept or broken, record the verdict on the group

rows.title: Mark a group in fulfilment
rows.story: order-sourcing locks the group to a node. The group moves from Promised to Locked and the assignment is linked to it.
rows.policy: Whenever a group is locked at a node, mark it in fulfilment

rows.title: Mark a group shipped
rows.story: order-sourcing reports the packages. The group becomes Shipped, and deliveries that arrived early are replayed so the group can close at once.
rows.policy: Whenever a group ships, mark it shipped and replay early deliveries

rows.title: Close a group on delivery
rows.story: A package is delivered. A group is Delivered once every package it announced is delivered. A package shared by merged groups closes all of them.
rows.policy: Whenever a package is delivered, mark it for every group that names it

rows.title: Mark a group lost or returned
rows.story: One lost package loses the group, and one returned package returns it. Both are final.
rows.policy: Whenever a package is lost or returned, mark its group lost or returned

rows.title: Show the delivery window of the day
rows.story: The carrier narrows a package to a time window on the day. It shows on the tracking view only; the promise and the order are untouched. A delivery point flagged as failing twice shows as a notice the same way.
rows.policy: Whenever a package gets a day-of window, show it unless a newer one is stored

hotspots.text: If delivery-promise is slow or down, checkout answers 503. There is no fallback promise, so the shopper must retry.
The cancel check is advisory. A lock this context has not yet consumed is invisible, so order-sourcing's answer decides.
A delivery can arrive before the shipment it belongs to. It is stored and replayed later; an unknown order is skipped, not retried.
A shopper whose consolidated offer expired is re-quoted without that tier. This is an accepted limitation.
The ship-to route is called restricted, but the fleet has no authentication and none is planned here.

opportunities.text: Storefront callers must accept the fifth (consolidated) tier before any shopper can be offered it.
The MCP tools and agent skills could later show the window's time zone, as the REST API does.
